_docblock: DELIBERATELY BROKEN CONTRACT MATERIAL — the bite proof for the node-contract gate.
A gate that cannot fail is not a gate. Every case below is a mutation of
fleet-node-contract.v1.json, one field at a time, in one direction at a time.
SAME harness functions the real conformance suite uses and asserts the harness
goes red — and red for the right REASON, because 'the platform now requires
something a deployed node cannot send' and 'a deployed node sends something the
platform now forbids' need different fixes and different people paged.
NOTHING HERE IS A CONTRACT. Do not copy a body out of this file into the
baseline. These shapes exist to be rejected.

requestCases.name: platform-too-new — a previously-optional field became required (the EW-792 shape)
requestCases.note: The literal body a node built before suspend-safe leases sends. Classified by the ABSENCE of the complained-about key from the body, not by the message text.

requestCases.name: platform-too-new — the complete verb requires a field an older node omits
node-too-old — a deployed node sends a self-description field the platform does not declare
requestCases.note: forbidNonWhitelisted turns an undeclared field into a 400. This is what a node ONE release ahead of the platform looks like — and what a rollback of a self-description field does to the whole fleet at once.

requestCases.name: node-too-old — an enroll body carrying a field a later platform removed
node-too-old — the lease poll gains a field the platform does not know

responseCases.name: a response field the node dereferences disappeared (enroll.secret)
responseCases.note: FleetClient.enroll throws `malformed` and the machine never stores a credential — it retries the one-time token forever and enrolls nothing.

responseCases.name: a response field changed type (node.id became a number)
responseCases.note: readNode() requires `typeof view.id === 'string'`; a numeric id is `malformed` on every beat.

responseCases.name: the lease job list became null instead of an empty array
responseCases.note: job-client.ts hard-throws `malformed` on anything that is not an array. This is the shape a well-meant 'return null when there is nothing' refactor produces, and it stops every node in the fleet leasing.

responseCases.name: the lease view dropped leaseGeneration
responseCases.note: Without it leaseGenerationOf() returns undefined, job-client omits the key, and every heartbeat and complete is 400'd by the DTO that requires it. One dropped response field, whole fleet stalled.

responseCases.name: the job heartbeat stopped sending ok
responseCases.note: Unlike the NODE heartbeat, the JOB heartbeat really does read `ok` — job-client.ts treats a missing one as `malformed`.

statusCases.name: enroll stopped answering 201
statusCases.note: The node only checks response.ok, so it would NOT notice — but apps/web/e2e/flow-fleet-enrollment-contract.spec.ts asserts 201, and any other client that branches on Created breaks silently. A status pin is the only thing that catches a change nobody's runtime complains about.

statusCases.name: the stale-lease refusal became a 401
statusCases.note: job-client maps 401 on a job heartbeat to null (lease lost, REPORT the failure) and 409 to `stale-lease` (abort, do NOT report). Swapping them makes a superseded run overwrite the state of whoever holds the job now.

statusCases.name: a stopped fleet started refusing the lease instead of answering empty
statusCases.note: Slice V's failure mode. Every node reads lease-401 as a revoked credential and goes `unauthorized`-sticky — a reversible global stop turns into a fleet-wide re-enrollment.
